Maszewo Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Maszewo, Poland

Demolished. This cemetery, probably established after 1812, was devastated during Kristallnacht in 1938, its monuments dismantled and trees cut down. Its last known burial was that of the elderly Louis Lübschütz in February 1933 — a funeral attended by only one Christian resident, the carpenter Richard Panzer, reflecting the changed relations between Jewish and Christian townspeople since Hitler's rise to power. On August 29, 2017, following the cemetery's 2016 entry into the national monuments register through the efforts of the Goleniów 'Biały Grosz' Historical Exploration Association, the plot's owner illegally commissioned bulldozers to level the site in connection with a planned development; the destruction was halted only after association chairman Wojciech Janda personally intervened, photographed the site, and stopped the excavator mid-operation, triggering an ongoing prosecutorial investigation. The recovered tombstones, secured at the local church, identify several of the deceased by name, including Mina Behrendt (1840–1913), Moses Behrendt (1815–1893), and Hugo Behrendt (died 1891).
